scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8155: EMERGENCY!! The big router for Campus 1, router16, the
edge one, is DEAD, and all of Campus 1's 172.16.10.x / 20.x / 30.x machines
have vanished for the rest of the network!! The Campus 1 people say things
still work inside their building, which makes me think something around
router16 is wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at router16 and
give Campus 1 back to us!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router16 is up: it holds its OSPF adjacencies
  (the mswitch0 uplink and the router7 link are Full), it has dynamic routes, and
  it forwards Campus 1 traffic to the rest of the network. A Campus 1 host reaches
  a Campus 2 host (e.g. 10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss. The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a core-router
  outage that is not occurring (cf. kath4-router16-ospfd-down, where router16's
  ospfd IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- router16 down, Campus 1
cut off -- is NOT reproducible: router16 is up with full OSPF neighbors (mswitch0
uplink and the router7 link in Full state), it has dynamic routes, and a Campus 1
host reaches Campus 2 (10.5.0.254) through router16 with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: router16 is healthy and forwarding,
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces a Campus
1 -> off-campus path through router16, finds it working, checks router16's OSPF
neighbors and that it is forwarding, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds"
a dead core router -- restarting router16 or blaming it to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Contrary to the ticket's claims, router16 is fully operational and Campus 1's 172.16.10.0/24, 172.16.20.0/24, and 172.16.30.0/24 networks are reachable from every tested external router.

Router16 has both uplinks active: bond0 (eth0+eth1 bonded, 10.2.2.1/24) connecting to mswitch0, and eth2 (172.30.1.1/24) connecting to router7. Both OSPF adjacencies are Full — router16 is DR on the 10.2.2.0/24 segment with mswitch0 as Backup, and participates as Backup DR on the 172.30.1.0/24 segment with router7 as DR. OSPF uptime for all router7 neighbors is approximately 6 minutes, identical to router7's other neighbors, confirming no recent flap — all adjacencies formed at lab startup.

mswitch0 serves as the Layer-3 gateway for all three campus VLANs: vlan10 (172.16.10.254/24), vlan20 (172.16.20.254/24), and vlan30 (172.16.30.254/24). It advertises these three stub networks into OSPF area 0 via its br0 uplink. Router16 propagates these LSAs to router7, which redistributes them further. Routes to 172.16.x appear in the RIB of router1, router7, router10, and router11. End-to-end pings from router10 to pc5 (172.16.10.5), router10 to pc10 (172.16.20.10), and router11 to pc12 (172.16.30.12) all succeed with zero packet loss. Campus PCs can also reach their default gateways.

Root cause: No fault exists. The ticket describes a symptom that is not reproducible — the network was either never broken or recovered during lab initialization before any diagnostic tests were run.

Corrective action: No configuration changes needed. Advise the reporter to retest from their workstation; if symptoms recur, capture specific source/destination hosts and timestamps for a new investigation.

The writeup's claims are consistent with those observations; minor DR-role wording is inferred from neighbor outputs but does not affect the overall diagnosis.
